Subject: Redwood SDK quickstart & env setup — next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of asks from Acme
- Validate SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) and a small sample app you can run locally
- Confirm auth model (API keys + optional service account/OIDC for Dedicated) and allowlist/networking requirements
- Proof-of-concept for embeddings + rerankers on a subset of your documents (~200k tokens)
- Guidance on structured outputs / tool-calling for the UI flow you demoed

Proposed next steps
1) I attached the Redwood SDK quickstart bundle (redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip) and a short networking checklist (networking-checklist.pdf). Please share these with Tom and your infra team.
2) Monica (cc'd) will prepare a 15-30 minute engineer-to-engineer call to walk through env setup, auth, and sample app run steps. Can we do Tue 2026-06-22 10:00am PT?
3) If you can share a small sample of documents or a subset of the data (S3 link or sample CSV), we'll prepare an embeddings/rerank cost estimate and a short eval to demonstrate quality.
4) We'll follow up with a mutual action plan and draft SOW after the technical call; sharing an initial MAP doc (acme-mutual-action-plan.docx).

Quick implementation notes (high level)
- SDKs: Python (pip install redwood-sdk) and TypeScript (npm i @redwoodai/sdk). Both support API key and bearer tokens; Dedicated customers can use short-lived OIDC tokens.
- Local testing: the quickstart includes a docker-compose that simulates requests with a local mock server. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or use local token file.
- Routing / structured output: we recommend starting with the redwood.chat.generate API and enabling structured output masks to enforce JSON schemas for tool-calling.
- Embeddings/rerank: we'll provide a sample pipeline (embed -> index -> rerank) and a small Jupyter notebook demonstrating scoring.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip, networking-checklist.pdf, acme-mutual-action-plan.docx

Please confirm Tue 10am PT or propose another slot. I’ll send the quick links + repo after you confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / Vivek —

I’ll own the engineer-to-engineer call and the quickstart repo prep. Notes for the sample app and what I’ll include in the repo:

Files I’ll add to redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip / repo:
- python/quickstart.py: minimal example calling redwood.text.generate and redwood.embeddings.embed
- typescript/src/index.ts: same flow using @redwoodai/sdk
- docker-compose.yml: local mock server + sample.env for REDWOOD_API_KEY
- notebooks/embeddings_demo.ipynb: pipeline for embed -> index -> rerank on small dataset
- README.md: env setup, API key vs OIDC, allowlist instructions

Auth and networking checklist (high level)
- API Key: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment (dev). Not recommended for production.
- OIDC/service accounts: we support OIDC tokens for Dedicated; the quickstart will include a sample token exchange script (service_account_token.sh).
- Allowlist: egress to api.redwood.ai (if using Hosted) or internal endpoints for Private. I attached networking-checklist.pdf with IP ranges and required ports.

Local testing instructions (short)
- Python: python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx && python python/quickstart.py
- TypeScript: npm ci && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx && npm run start:local
- No Docker required for basic examples; Docker-compose will help simulate latency and a local mock server if desired.

Embeddings sizing guidance
- For 200k tokens: expect ~X tokens/embedding call depending on chunking. I’ll run a quick sample to give a cost estimate before Tue call.

I’ll push the repo to the GH link and drop the shared Drive link in the calendar invite.

Monica
